authority.note: DESIGN.md is a pointer plus delta. The normative system is docs/15-design-system.md refined by docs/21-visual-language.md (21 wins on disagreement); normative token values live in src/app/globals.css under 'Fairfame Design System'. This sidecar records only what the marketing front door at / added or taught.

indigo-600.purpose: Interaction and nothing else — the primary CTA, action numerals, the evidence disclosure link, the short rule above a margin note.

indigo-100.purpose: The .marketing ::selection background. Ink-900 stays at full contrast on top of it.

ink-900.purpose: Both dark passages on the landing page — the masthead bar and the conscience band — and the app's navigation rail and briefing bar. The front door is ink so it reads as a piece of the application.

ink-800.purpose: Foreground text everywhere, and the margin note's title at full ink.

ink-600.purpose: Subheads, section intros, the artefact's summary, and quoted customer sentences.

ink-350.purpose: Every margin note body and every secondary description. The lightest ink that clears WCAG AA on a tinted surface (5.06:1 on white, 4.73:1 on --canvas) — ink-400 measures 4.37:1 on --canvas and is illegal here.

ink-300.purpose: Non-text only, and only on white — the quote glyph, the arrow between two figures. 3.06:1 on white; using it for a timestamp is an accessibility bug.

canvas.purpose: The page. Faintly tinted so white hairline cards have an edge without a shadow.

surface.purpose: Every container — briefing card, pricing table, score tile, disclosure notice.

line.purpose: The 1px border that does the job a shadow would do elsewhere.

line-soft.purpose: Between action rows in the artefact, and above every item in the delivery and product lists.

line-inner.purpose: Between cells inside one card — the artefact's header from its action list, one pricing column from the next.

amber-500.purpose: Ratings only. On the landing page it appears in exactly one place — the stars beside a quoted customer sentence — and nowhere in the page's chrome. There is no amber button and no amber surface here.

poster.purpose: The marketing front door only. The one fluid role in the scale, because it spans the viewport rather than a 1280px content column and must survive 390px to 1920px. Clamped at 68px (two lines of Turkish is the practical limit) and at 36px (below which it stops outranking the briefing card). Never inside the app.

hero.purpose: Public surfaces only — the conscience band's heading and the closing call.

display.purpose: Section headings on the landing page, and the artefact's own headline — deliberately one step below the page's poster so it does not compete with the argument about it.

metric-lg.purpose: The reputation score in the artefact's score tile. One per surface.

metric.purpose: The two figures the week actually moved, set as figures rather than buried in a clause.

lead.purpose: A sentence that is the subject of its row — the page subhead, an action's text, the closing paragraph.

title.purpose: Every card heading, every button, every definition term.

body.purpose: Page body and the conscience band's paragraphs.

copy.purpose: Body inside a card — the margin note title and body, quoted customer sentences, the disclosure summary.

meta.purpose: Timestamps, the no-card note, the evidence intro, the price cadence.

shadows.name: none-on-cards
shadows.purpose: Hairline first. Every container on the marketing page carries a 1px --line border and no shadow. This is not an app-only rule.

shadows.name: elevation-md
shadows.purpose: The only shadow on the landing page, and only on the skip-to-content link when it takes focus. Two shadows per step — a tight contact one that reads as an edge and a wide ambient one that reads as height; a single blur at any radius reads as a smudge.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system's only easing. No springs, no bounce.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Anything that moves, including the evidence disclosure.

motion.name: evidence-in
motion.value: @keyframes evidence-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-2px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
motion.purpose: The landing page's one authored motion moment: an action's evidence opening. docs/15 §4 forbids entrance animation on data, and this is read for what it says — it forbids decorating arrival, and this is not arrival, it is the immediate answer to a disclosure the reader pressed. 180ms, two pixels, and disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: spread-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: The annotated spread collapses at lg, not md: below roughly 1024px a 17rem margin squeezed to 9rem stops reading as apparatus and starts reading as a second, narrower body.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The page's one filled control — 'open the sample briefing', in the first viewport and again at the close.

components.name: Margin Note
components.description: The signature pattern: an annotation beside the element it explains. No box, no border, no fill — a short indigo rule, a title at full ink, a body at the lightest legal ink on canvas.

components.description: The page's one interaction. A native details/summary — no JavaScript, no ARIA, keyboard-operable for free, works with scripts off, stays open. The page never links away to prove a claim.

components.name: Hairline Card
components.description: Every container on the page. 14px corner, 1px --line border, white, and no shadow — depth comes from the tinted canvas behind it, never from elevation.
components.html:
Kadıköy Kahve · Merkez · son 7 gün

Temizlik bu hafta üç kez geçti

Yorum hacmi sabit kaldı, ancak olumsuzların yarısı aynı konuya işaret ediyor.

components.name: Action Row
components.description: One of the three things to do this week. An indigo circled numeral, the action at lead size, and its evidence beneath. The numeral is deliberately not monospaced — a numeral in a circle is not code, data or a measurement.
components.html:

components.name: Score Tile
components.description: The reputation score, in the same shape and ink the dashboard uses. Never banded by threshold — indigo means interactive and amber means a rating, and a composed 0–100 score is neither. Absence renders as a sentence, never an em-dash.

narrative.overview:
Fairfame's system was built entirely for Operate surfaces — a review queue, a dashboard, an analytics workspace — where the reader already believes the product and needs to work. The landing page at / is the first Persuade surface, and it was built without softening a single rule: same tokens, same hairlines, same refusal of imagery. The delta is therefore small on purpose. One new type role, one scoped stylesheet block, and one new layout pattern.

The page's thesis is that it IS the artefact. It renders a real weekly briefing from getSampleDigest() — the same pipeline, arithmetic and model that runs on a customer's own reviews — and puts the marketing argument in the margins beside it, each note anchored to the element it explains. It refuses the category arrangement of a slogan over a device-framed screenshot followed by three feature cards, and it refuses it structurally: there is no screenshot to frame and no card grid to fill.

Two things carried across from Operate that a marketing surface would normally abandon, and both held. Zero raster — docs/15 §7's 'the product's imagery is its data' survives on a surface whose category default is photography, and the built page contains no photograph, illustration, gradient or texture of any kind. And hairline-first — the briefing card, the pricing table and the disclosure notice all carry a 1px --line border and no shadow, on a page where floating cards are the convention.
keyCharacteristics: Marginalia instead of feature cards; the argument sits beside its evidence, never three screens from it.
One fluid type role, and it exists only here.
Evidence discloses in place; the page never links away to prove a claim.
The artefact is composed live, not screenshotted.
Alternating density: an annotated spread, then a quiet full-width section that earns it.

rules.name: The No-Amber-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Amber is a rating colour and nothing else on this surface. There is no amber button, no amber surface and no amber highlight anywhere on /, but the star ratings inside the evidence disclosure render in the system's amber, because Stars is amber by default and a rating drawn in ink would be a different lie. (The direction contract's OWN-WORLD line reads 'no amber' flatly; the build diverges, correctly. Amber on a rating is native to this world and banning it would have meant repainting the one mark the product treats as pictographic.)

rules.name: The Marketing Selection Rule
rules.body: .marketing ::selection is indigo at its lightest tint (indigo-100) with ink-900 on top. Scoped to .marketing rather than set globally: a selection colour that suits a landing page is not automatically the right one behind a review queue somebody drags a cursor through all day.

rules.name: The Poster Rule
rules.body: --text-poster is the only fluid role in the scale, and it is fluid because it is the only role that spans the viewport rather than a 1280px content column — it has to survive 390px to 1920px, where every other role lives at a predictable measure. It is clamped so it cannot exceed 68px or drop below 36px, the point at which it stops outranking the briefing card beneath it. Never use it inside the app: a dashboard has one subject and display names it.

rules.name: The Artefact-Does-Not-Shout Rule
rules.body: The briefing card's own headline is set at display, not hero, precisely because the page's headline above it is at poster. An artefact that shouts as loudly as the page is an artefact competing with its own argument.

rules.name: The Registered-Role Rule
rules.body: Adding a --text-* token means adding it to FONT_SIZES in src/lib/utils.ts, or cn() silently drops the size and the element falls back to 16px. --text-poster is registered; tests/lib/class-merge.test.ts fails if the next one is not.

rules.name: The Alternating Density Rule
rules.body: An annotated spread is the page's dense passage; a full-width section with no margin note is the quiet one that earns it. Two annotated sections in a row exhaust the device, and two identical two-column lists in a row read as one section repeated — which is why delivery is four across and the product areas are six in two-to-three columns. Absence of a margin note is rhythm, never omission.

rules.name: The Marginalia-Means-One-Thing Rule
rules.body: A margin note glosses the artefact. It must not degenerate into a second column of body copy, which is what happens the moment every section gets one.

dos: Do treat docs/15 + docs/21 as the authority and DESIGN.md as the delta. A rule that belongs to the whole product goes there, not here.
Do use --text-poster on the marketing front door and nowhere else; register any new --text-* role in FONT_SIZES.
Do scope a Persuade-only stylesheet rule under .marketing. Motion and selection colour chosen for a landing page are not automatically right behind a review queue.
Do compose the artefact live from the real pipeline. A picture of a briefing forfeits the entire claim the page makes.
Do derive commercial copy from what the product enforces — the pricing table diffs PLAN_CATALOG, so the page is wrong only when the product is wrong.

Do label an invented business as invented, above the artefact and in full ink, and make the claim conditional on what actually happened: when the model was unreachable and the briefing fell back to written prose, the sentence asserting 'same model, same arithmetic' must change with it.
Do keep ink-350 as the floor for text on --canvas; ink-400 is legal on white cards only.
donts: Don't put a margin note beside every section. Its meaning is 'a gloss on the artefact', and it survives only while that is true.
Don't give a margin note a border, a fill or a card. The absence of a box IS the pattern.
Don't make the annotated spread collapse at md. A 17rem margin squeezed to 9rem is a second body column, not an annotation.
Don't add a shadow to a marketing card. Hairline-first is not an app-only rule.
Don't introduce photography, illustration, gradient or texture on a marketing surface. docs/15 §7 holds here; the category default does not override it.
Don't link away to prove a claim. Evidence opens in place.
Don't set the artefact's own headline at poster or hero to match the page. It is the subject, not the argument.
